claims.evidence: The accession-scoped Raw_files.zip directory contains GA4, GA5 and GA6 .d members, each with an analysis.tdf and SampleInfo.xml whose method name begins Proteome_DDA_PASEF.
Each accession-matched SampleInfo.xml contains the exact Bruker SampleID and maps to the corresponding .d directory. PRIDE describes PCLS supernatant as the study material.
PRIDE identifies rat organism and lung organ; paper describes rat precision-cut lung slices.

claims.value: Lys-C; fixed carbamidomethyl C, variable oxidation M/P and protein N-terminal acetyl; 20 ppm precursor and 15 ppm fragment tolerance
claims.evidence: The deposited 2021-12-02 processing log lists all three GA4/GA5/GA6 runs in one FragPipe group. Each run-specific pepXML search_summary independently reports LysC, fixed C +57.0215, variable M and P +15.9949, variable protein N-terminal +42.0106, ±20 ppm precursor and 15 ppm fragment tolerance. These run-specific outputs outrank the project-level PRIDE prose mentioning lysine acetylation and the archived GUI config, whose fragment tolerance differs from the actual search output.

limitations: No run-level table identifies the solvent, experimental condition, tissue donor, or whether these three run IDs are biological or technical replicates. Each deposited Bruker SampleID is therefore a distinct source name with biological replicate 1, and no factor value is asserted.

PRIDE also describes peptidome runs; this SDRF covers only the three archived runs whose Bruker method explicitly says Proteome_DDA_PASEF. The nine peptidome acquisitions require separate technical settings.
The article full text was not accessible from the available endpoints; PRIDE protocols, deposited Bruker XML, and FragPipe configuration supply the granular metadata.
Some processed search filenames name acquisitions absent from Raw_files.zip; they are excluded from this raw-acquisition SDRF.

The deposited 2021-12-02 GUI config lists 20 ppm fragment tolerance, while all three run-specific pepXML files list 15 ppm; the latter is used. PRIDE prose says lysine acetylation, while the run-specific pepXML files list protein N-terminal acetylation; the run-specific search output is used.
